Short-acting beta2 agonists are used as bronchodilators in patients with chron- ic obstructive pulmonary disease (see p.1112), although there is some evidence to suggest that an antimuscarinic might be prefer- able. Guidelines indicate that long-acting beta2 agonists such as salmeterol may be used for maintenance therapy in moderate and more severe disease. Improvement in lung function and symp- toms has been seen in such patients after regular treatment with inhaled salmeterol;1-3 a reduction in exacerbations has also been seen.4 Additional benefit has been reported from the use of salm- eterol with inhaled corticosteroids.5-7 1.
